# Test fixtures

## `game-401729745.json.gz`
A real `ProcessedGame` — the exact body the Python API serves for
`GET /cfb/401729745/process` (North Dakota State at Abilene Christian, 2024
week 15, Final; 176 plays, 26 drives, advanced box score). ~3 MB raw, gzipped.

**Provenance (2026-09-01):** generated offline on `sdv-data` by running the
Flask app in `python/` through its test client with `sportsdataverse.cfb.cfb_pbp.download`
patched to return the captured ESPN summary at
`cfbfastR-cfb-raw/cfb/json/raw/401729745.json` (plus `play_participants` and
`game_rosters` from the same repo). No network; no hand edits. Odds override was
not passed (the raw repo's betting shape differs), so `pickcenter`/spread come
from the summary itself.

**Used by:** `test/gamePage.render.test.ts`, which feeds it through
`retrieveProcessedGame` (mocked `wrappedFetch`) and renders `GamePage` with the
Astro Container API.

**To regenerate** after a parser change: repeat the above against the same raw
JSON; the game id must stay the same so the test's URL/JSON-LD assertions hold.

## `game-401772944-nfl.json.gz`
A real NFL `ProcessedGame` — the exact body the Python API serves for
`GET /nfl/401772944/process` (Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos, 2025 REG
week 10, Final; 175 plays, advanced box score with all 8 sections). ~2.8 MB
raw, gzipped.

**Provenance (2026-09-09):** generated by running the Flask app in `python/`
through its test client (`app.app.test_client()`) against ESPN's live summary
for the game, on the droplet. No hand edits. `success` on each play is the
route's own derivation (EPA > 0) — `NFLPlayProcess` does not emit it.

**Used by:** `test/nflGamePage.render.test.ts` (mirror of the CFB render test
with `locals.league = 'nfl'`).

**To regenerate:** same call; the game id must stay 401772944 so the test's
URL assertions hold.

## `game-401752696.json.gz`
A real `ProcessedGame` for `GET /cfb/401752696/process` (Wisconsin at Alabama,
2025-09-13, Final 14-38; 131 plays). Its last snap is the losing AWAY team's
(Danny O'Neil run for 8), the case the old Game Excitement Index rule got wrong.

**Provenance (2026-10-08):** generated by running the Flask app in `python/`
through its test client (`app.app.test_client()`) against ESPN's live summary,
on the droplet, with the `uv.lock` pin (sportsdataverse 0.1.4, `01d3c1a`). No
hand edits.

**Used by:** `test/gei.test.ts`, beside the two game fixtures above (both end on
the winning home team's kneel-down).

**To regenerate:** same call; keep a game whose final play belongs to the away
team, or the test's possession assertion fails.

## `pregame-401872933-nfl.json.gz`, `pregame-401858458-cfb.json.gz`
The two ESPN payloads a *scheduled* game page reads, per league, in one object:
`{ playbyplay, summary }`.

- NFL: Carolina at Atlanta (401872933), 2026 week 3 — `STATUS_SCHEDULED`.
- CFB: Purdue at UCLA (401858458), 2026 week 4 — `STATUS_SCHEDULED`.

**Provenance (2026-09-19):** captured verbatim, no hand edits, from
`cdn.espn.com/core/<espnPath>/playbyplay?gameId=<id>&xhr=1&render=false&userab=18`
(the body `retrieveGamePage` returns) and
`site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/football/<espnPath>/summary?event=<id>`
(the body `retrieveGameSummary` returns: `gameInfo.venue`, `pickcenter`,
`lastFiveGames`).

**Used by:** `test/preGamePage.render.test.ts`, which renders `PreGamePage` for
both leagues with the SDV client mocked. The game page tests next door use
*final* games, so before this fixture `PreGamePage` never rendered in the suite.

**To regenerate:** re-capture both URLs for a scheduled game; keep the ids, the
teams (ESPN ids 1/29 and 26/2509) and the scheduled status, which the test's
logo, venue and link assertions name.

## `nfl-summaries-2025.json`
Real rows from the published `nfl_team_summaries` / `nfl_passing` 2025 assets
(the nfl-data stage-06 producer's 2026-09-10 rebuild, which added
`series_conv_off/def` and `fourth_decisions_off_rank`): the top-4 teams by net
adjusted EPA from `team_summaries` (all 421 columns) and the top-4 qualified
passers by TEPA rank from `passing`. Captured 2026-09-10; no hand edits. The `team_summaries` rows were re-cut
2026-09-18 from the same 2025 `nfl_model_pbp` with nfl-data's
`yardsplay`-denominator fix (`fix/team-summaries-yardsplay-denominator`), which
moves the 27 columns that read `yards_gained` (`yardsplay_*`, `play_stuffed_*`,
`havoc_*` and their ranks); every other column is byte-identical to the
published asset. The published asset follows that fix's merge, so until it is
rebuilt this fixture leads it on those columns.

**Used by:** `test/nflLeaderboards.render.test.ts` and `test/explicitRoutes.test.ts`, which mock the SDV client
with these rows and render the team and
player leaderboard pages with `locals.league = 'nfl'`.

## `nfl-coaches-2024.json`
Real rows from the nfl-data head-coach tendency builder, 2024: the full
`team_tendencies` (32 teams), `coach_tendencies` (32 head-coach seasons) and
`coach_careers` (42 coaches, 2023–2024 pooled) payloads as the SDV Data API
returns them (`{data: [...]}` bodies, one key per table; every one of the 266
columns). Captured 2026-09-15 from the builder's parquet output; no hand edits.
The careers rows include interim stints under the 1,500-play floor (Giff Smith,
208 plays; Chris Tabor, 377), which is what the min-plays divider test needs.

**Used by:** `test/coaches.test.ts` (every board column resolves to a column the
payload carries; sort/rank/format contracts) and
`test/coachLeaderboards.render.test.ts`, which mocks the SDV client with these
rows and renders the season and careers boards for both leagues.

**To regenerate** after a builder change: re-export the three tables for 2024
and replace the arrays; keep 2024 so the render test's URL assertions hold.

## `player-cfb-4433971-2024.json` / `player-nfl-16800-2024.json`
The exact bodies the Data API's player-keyed routes return for one player each
(sdv-db #71): `identity` (`/v1/{league}/players/{espn id}`), `seasons`
(`…/seasons`, **every** season, which is what the career roll-up needs), `games`
and `splits` for 2024, and the 404 body for an unknown id.

* **CFB** — Kyle McCord (ESPN 4433971), 2024 Syracuse: passing *and* rushing box
  categories in one game, four seasons of season rows across two schools, and a
  postseason game whose schedule `week` restarts at 1 (which is why the game log
  orders on the kickoff date).
* **NFL** — Davante Adams (ESPN 16800, gsis `00-0031381`), 2024: traded LV → NYJ,
  so two team-season rows, reachable from the ESPN id only through the nflverse
  crosswalk. The 27-play LV stint is under the producer's qualification gate and
  carries null `_rank`/`_pct`; the 114-play NYJ row carries both.

**Provenance (2026-09-19):** captured on the droplet by mounting sdv-db's
`player_routes.add_player_routes` on a bare FastAPI app over the live read engine
and calling each route through `TestClient`. No hand edits, no trimming.

**Used by:** `test/players.test.ts` (the reconciliation arithmetic: the game log
sums to the `all` split, the split groups partition it, the roll-up rates
recompute) and `test/playerPages.render.test.ts` (the render contract for every
table on `/players/[id]` and its `/nfl` twin).

**To regenerate** after a route change: repeat the above for the same two ids and
seasons — the render test asserts on those ids, teams and dates.

## `usage-cfb-400869270.json.gz` / `usage-nfl-401872922.json.gz`
Real `ProcessedGame` payloads — the exact bodies the Python API serves for
`GET /cfb/400869270/process` (CMU at OKST, 2016 week 2, Final) and
`GET /nfl/401872922/process` (CLE at JAX, 2026 REG week 1, Final). Unlike the two
`game-*.json.gz` fixtures these carry **every** `advBoxScore` section the game
page can render — the usage / tackles / special-teams sections
(`sportsdataverse.football.usage_box`) and a fitted `paperIndex` — at a tenth
of the size, because the games are smaller.

**Provenance (2026-09-18):** produced offline, no network, by driving
`python/app.py`'s `/<league>/<id>/process` through the Flask test client with
the processors replaced by the `_OfflineNFL` / `_OfflineCFB` subclasses in
`python/tests/test_usage_box_route.py`, which read the ESPN summaries (and, for
the NFL, the core play items) already committed under `python/tests/fixtures`.
No hand edits. The NFL game carries play participants, so its tackle and
position-group sections are populated; the CFB game has none, so those sections
are legitimately empty.

**Used by:** `test/tableDecisions.render.test.ts` — the render-level guards for
the table-reconciliation decisions (#264 review).

**To regenerate** after a processor change: re-run that same offline route call
for both leagues and overwrite the files; the game ids must stay the same.

Regenerated 2026-10-07 after python/paper_index.add_start_ep (G10): drives rows carry avg_start_ep; same offline call. It also picks up the processor pin's changes since the first capture (win probabilities, the NFL tackle-points columns), and the teams' row order within a section can differ from one run to the next, so tests key rows by team id rather than by position.

**Used by:** `test/tableContracts.render.test.ts` — the render-level table
contract, twin-parity and aggregation-reconciliation tests (plan V3b).

## `coach-situations.json`
Real rows from the live Data API, captured 2026-11-02: head-coach (`role=HC`) `coach_tendencies` for CFB 2025
(125) and NFL 2024 (32), and `coach_careers` for CFB (447) and NFL (165), each trimmed by `select` to the key
columns plus the game-context columns the Situations board reads (`games_` / `wins_` / `win_rate_` for
`after_bye`, `opener`, `one_score_game`, and in CFB `vs_ranked` with `epa_per_play_vs_ranked` /
`def_epa_per_play_vs_ranked`). No hand edits. The NFL careers hold Bill Callahan (2,785 plays, 0 openers,
`win_rate_opener` null), which is what the zero-openers test needs; the NFL tables carry no `*_vs_ranked` column
(asking for one is a 400).

**Used by:** `test/coaches.test.ts` (situations block) and `test/coachLeaderboards.render.test.ts`.

**To regenerate**, from `astro/`, in one shell call so `SDV_AUTH_TOKEN` never leaves it:

```bash
SDV_AUTH_TOKEN="$(grep -E '^SDV_AUTH_TOKEN=' .dev.vars | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d "\"'")" \
node --input-type=module -e '
const base = "https://data.sportsdataverse.org/v1";
const get = async (p) => {
  const r = await fetch(`${base}/${p}`, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SDV_AUTH_TOKEN}` } });
  if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`${p}: ${r.status}`);
  return (await r.json()).data;
};
const ctx = (l) => (l === "cfb" ? ["after_bye", "opener", "one_score_game", "vs_ranked"] : ["after_bye", "opener", "one_score_game"]);
const metrics = (l) => [...ctx(l).flatMap((c) => [`games_${c}`, `wins_${c}`, `win_rate_${c}`]), ...(l === "cfb" ? ["epa_per_play_vs_ranked", "def_epa_per_play_vs_ranked"] : [])];
const season = ["season", "pos_team_id", "pos_team", "coach", "role", "games", "plays", "drives"];
const career = ["coach", "role", "teams", "seasons", "first_season", "last_season", "games", "plays", "drives"];
const sel = (keys, l) => [...keys, ...metrics(l)].join(",");
const out = {
  cfb_coach_tendencies_2025: await get(`cfb/coach_tendencies?season=2025&role=HC&select=${sel(season, "cfb")}&limit=500`),
  cfb_coach_careers: await get(`cfb/coach_careers?role=HC&select=${sel(career, "cfb")}&limit=2000`),
  nfl_coach_tendencies_2024: await get(`nfl/coach_tendencies?season=2024&role=HC&select=${sel(season, "nfl")}&limit=500`),
  nfl_coach_careers: await get(`nfl/coach_careers?role=HC&select=${sel(career, "nfl")}&limit=2000`),
};
(await import("node:fs")).writeFileSync("test/fixtures/coach-situations.json", JSON.stringify(out, null, 1) + "\n");
for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(out)) console.log(k, v.length);
'
```

## `neighbors-ranked-rows.json`
Real rows from the live Data API, captured 2026-09-26: every team's six
nearby-rank metrics and ranks (NFL 2025, CFB 2024) and every ranked row of NFL 2024 receiving and CFB 2024 passing
(`<metric>_rank >= 1`). No hand edits. NFL 2024 receiving holds Davante Adams' NYJ row (ranked) but not his LV row
(under the qualifier), which is what the traded-player tests need.

**Used by:** `test/neighbors.test.ts`, `test/rankNeighbors.render.test.ts`, `test/playerPages.render.test.ts`.

**To regenerate**, from `astro/`, in one shell call so `SDV_AUTH_TOKEN` (read from `.dev.vars`) never
leaves it; keep the seasons so the tests' ids (NFL team 14, CFB passer 4433971, gsis `00-0031381`) hold:

```bash
SDV_AUTH_TOKEN="$(grep -E '^SDV_AUTH_TOKEN=' .dev.vars | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d "\"'")" \
node --input-type=module -e '
const base = "https://data.sportsdataverse.org/v1";
const get = async (p) => {
  const r = await fetch(`${base}/${p}`, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SDV_AUTH_TOKEN}` } });
  if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`${p}: ${r.status}`);
  return (await r.json()).data;
};
const T = ["net_adj_epa","EPAplay_off","success_off","explosive_off","EPAplay_def","success_def"];
const tsel = ["team_id","pos_team","season","conference", ...T, ...T.map((m) => `${m}_rank`)].join(",");
const psel = (name, ms) => ["player_id", name, "team_id", "pos_team", "season", ...ms, ...ms.map((m) => `${m}_rank`)].join(",");
const out = {
  nfl_team_summaries_2025: await get(`nfl/team_summaries?season=2025&select=${tsel}&limit=150`),
  cfb_team_summaries_2024: await get(`cfb/team_summaries?season=2024&select=${tsel}&limit=150`),
  nfl_receiving_2024: await get(`nfl/receiving?season=2024&select=${psel("receiver_player_name", ["EPAplay","success","yardsplay","TEPA"])}&EPAplay_rank__gte=1&order=EPAplay_rank&limit=1000`),
  cfb_passing_2024: await get(`cfb/passing?season=2024&select=${psel("passer_player_name", ["EPAplay","success","yardsdropback","TEPA"])}&EPAplay_rank__gte=1&order=EPAplay_rank&limit=1000`),
};
(await import("node:fs")).writeFileSync("test/fixtures/neighbors-ranked-rows.json", JSON.stringify(out, null, 1) + "\n");
for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(out)) console.log(k, v.length);
'
```

## `team-summaries-cfb-2025.json` / `team-summaries-nfl-2025.json`
The Data API's `GET /v1/{cfb|nfl}/team_summaries?season=2025&limit=200` bodies
(every team: 136 CFB, 32 NFL), trimmed by `select` to `team_id`, `pos_team`,
`season` and the 30 Five Factors value columns (`fiveFactorColumns()`, in table
order) followed by their `_rank`s. Ranks are Float64 with ties averaged, so some
are `x.5` (Auburn's `turnovers_off_rank` is 13.5).

**Provenance (2026-09-30):** captured from the live API after the 2025 team
summaries were rebuilt with cfbfastR-cfb-data#115 / nfl-data#72 (per-drive
`start_position`, drive start EP, havoc margin and EPA, expected turnovers and
turnover luck) and sdv-db#102 added those columns to the API's schema snapshot;
rows sorted by `team_id`, no other edits.

**Used by:** `test/fiveFactors.test.ts` (every `FIVE_FACTORS` key and its `_rank`
exist) and `test/fiveFactors.render.test.ts` (the panel's cells on
`/year/2025/team/333` and `/nfl/year/2025/team/12`, and the tied rank on
`/year/2025/team/2`).

**To regenerate:** repeat the same `select` for 2025; the render test asserts on
teams 333 and 2 (CFB) and 12 (NFL).

- `nba/*.json`: the first 2,000 Nets rows of the real `nba_stats_shots/shots_2026.parquet` (2026-09-30) and both teams' rows for their 24 games, plus blazing-the-nets `lib/` outputs on those rows (its `scripts/dump-oracle.mjs`).

  **To regenerate:** these are not Data API rows (the route tests build API-shaped rows from them
  in-test). In a blazing-the-nets checkout at the commit `src/nba/PROVENANCE.md` cites, run
  `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/dump-oracle.mjs <out-dir>`: it reads blazing's committed
  `test/fixtures/shots_2026_bkn_2000.parquet` and `game_logs_2026_bkn.parquet` plus the live
  `player_season_stats_2026.parquet` release (season 2026, regular season, the fixture's players).
  Copy `shots.json`, `game_logs.json`, `league_context.json`, `season_players.json` and
  `player_games.json` here; `player_season_stats.json` and its `README.md` are not used.
- `season_players_2026_api.json`: every `shot_season_players` row for 2026, straight from the Data API
  (`GET /v1/nba_stats/shot_season_players?season=2026&limit=50000`, bearer token required; `.data` only).
  Captured 2026-10-11. Regenerate with the same request; the rows change nightly during the season.

## `team-opponent-splits-2025.json`
The Data API bodies the season team page's Results by Opponent panel reads, for
Alabama (`cfb`, 333) and Kansas City (`nfl`, 12), keyed by league:
`team_id` (`GET /v1/{league}/team_opponent_splits?season=2025&team_id=<id>`),
`opponent_id` (the same with `opponent_id=<id>`: each opponent's row against
the team) and `schedule.home_id` / `schedule.away_id` (the two schedule reads
`retrieveTeamSchedule` makes: `cfb` `schedule`, `nfl` `espn_schedule`, with
`order=-start_date`). CFB rows carry `opponent` and cover FCS opponents and
the postseason (two postseason week-1 games); NFL rows carry no name and are
regular season only.

`cfb_155` holds the same six reads for North Dakota (FCS, `cfb` 155), whose
2025 rows cover two games. Its Margin view's season average (-0.124 EPA/play,
offense and defense each weighted by their own plays) sits beyond both bars
(-0.09, -0.10): the real case that the chart's value axis must include the
average line.

**Provenance (2026-10-08):** captured verbatim from the live API; no edits.

**Used by:** `test/gameSet.test.ts` (bar order, labels, raw and margin values,
play-weighted averages) and `test/gameSet.render.test.ts` (the panel on
`/year/2025/team/333` and `/nfl/year/2025/team/12`, its island props, the gates).

**To regenerate:** repeat the six reads for 2025; the tests assert on those
teams' games, labels and scores.

**Used by:** `test/gameSet.test.ts` (one `GAME_METRICS` entry per rate column, each

**To regenerate:** repeat the six reads for 2026. The values move with every

## `schedule-nfl-6-2025.json`
The same two bodies for Dallas's 2025 season, an NFL record with a tie: `home_id`
is `GET /v1/nfl/espn_schedule?season=2025&home_id=6&order=-start_date` and
`away_id` the same with `away_id`. Every column, no `select`.

**Provenance (2026-10-10):** chosen by scanning the full 2025 `nfl/espn_schedule`
(`?season=2025&limit=400`, 285 games) for a completed game with equal scores. The
only one is game 401772921, week 4, Green Bay at Dallas, 40-40, `STATUS_FINAL`,
both `*_winner` false (2024 has none). Captured verbatim from the live API by the
same script that reproduces `schedule-nfl-12-2025.json` byte for byte; one row per
line, no other edits.

**Used by:** `test/resume.test.ts` (the tie is a third number in Overall, Home and
One-score; Home + Away partition it; `retrieveTeamSeasonInformation` prints the
same `7-9-1`, with a `4-2` division record) and `test/resume.render.test.ts` (the
Record panel on `/nfl/year/2025/team/6`, and the TeamCard's `7-9-1 (Div: 4-2)`).

**To regenerate:** repeat both calls for 2025; the tests assert Dallas's 7-9-1
(4-3-1 at home, 3-6 away).

- `nba/game_401766458_processor.json` and `nba/game_401766458_api.json`: one game (Atlanta at Orlando, 2025-04-15 play-in, final 95-120, 496 plays) from both sources, the parity gate for `NbaGame` (`test/nba/game.test.ts`). Captured 2026-10-11.

## `team-season-percentiles-cfb.json`
The Data API's `GET https://data.sportsdataverse.org/v1/cfb/team_summaries/percentiles`
body (no `season`: every season, oldest first), trimmed: of the 598 rows (23
seasons x 26 metrics) it keeps the 12 for seasons 2023-2025 and metrics
`EPAplay_off`, `EPAplay_margin`, `success_off_pass` and `havoc_def`, and `count`
is set to 12 to match. Each row is untouched: `{season, metric, teams, breaks[101]}`.

**Provenance (2026-10-18):** captured from the live API with the read key, the
day sdv-db #171 deployed the route. 2024 `EPAplay_off`: 134 teams, breaks[1|25|50|75|99]
= -0.172 / -0.023 / 0.035 / 0.096 / 0.218.

**Used by:** `test/teamSeasonBands.test.ts` (the flatten/validate mapping, the
404 case, the profile route with the `team-season-bands` flag on and off) and
`test/teamTrendBands.test.ts` (the metric filter).

**To regenerate:** repeat the request and apply the same trim.

(`https://data.sportsdataverse.org`) with the read key. Trimmed to three of the 24

The same route with a position group:

The envelope adds `position_group`; the rows are the same shape, over the QB
roster group's player-seasons only (480 in `all`, 217 in `red_zone`).

**Provenance (2026-10-18):** fetched from the live Data API
(`https://data.sportsdataverse.org`) with the read key. Trimmed to three of the 24
rows (`all/epa`, `all/epa_per_play`, `red_zone/epa`) and `count` set to 3; the rows
themselves are untouched. (The TE group's response that day had 20 rows: no
`red_zone`, under the route's 30 player-season minimum, which is the per-split
fallback `loadSplitBreaks` handles.)

**Used by:** `test/playerSplitPercentiles.test.ts` (the `position_group` request
and its mapping).

## `standings-cfb-8-2026.json.gz`, `standings-cfb-37-2026.json.gz`, `standings-nfl-8-2026.json.gz`
Real ESPN CFB standings bodies, `site.api.espn.com/apis/v2/sports/football/college-football/standings?group=<id>`,
for the SEC (8: 16 entries on the group itself) and the Sun Belt (37: no entries on the group; its 7+7 teams sit on

`lineups-nba-2025.json.gz` from #402 (BB-G3), whose sections in those PRs give the provenance. In short: sdv-db's committed
producer output `tests/fixtures/season_products/nba_player_{on_off,wowy}_2025.parquet` (sdv-db #198) for the Minnesota
Timberwolves 2024-25 (`team_id` 1610612750, 20 players, 190 pairs), and Minnesota's live `shot_season_players` name rows.

would carry it, and applies the API's own filters (`player_id`, `player_id_a`, `player_id_b`, `order`, `limit`). The
player is Anthony Edwards (1630162). Nothing else is edited.

**Used by:** `test/playerOnOff.test.ts`.

`player_on_off?season=2026&player_id=<id>&order=-minutes_on&limit=5` and `player_wowy?season=2026&player_id_a=<id>&limit=100`
(and `player_id_b=`) reads replace them.

## `garbage-time-{nba-0022300718,wbb-401824983,wnba-1022600001,nba-0022600001}.json.gz`
One game's possession log with BB-D7's flags and sportsdataverse-py's own situational splits for that game, the oracle
for BB-G2's garbage-time toggle (`utils/garbageTime.ts`). Built on 2026-11-08 with sportsdataverse-py `origin/main`
64b22369 from the sportsdataverse-data releases (no Data API read), as `{league, game_id, espnGameId, note, teams,
possessions, oracle, names}`:

- **The pros** (`load_{nba,wnba}_stats_possessions`, `_pbp`, `_schedules`, filtered to the game): `possessions` is the
  release's rows with `nba_possession_flags.add_possession_flags` appended (`seconds_to_first_shot`, `is_transition`,
  `is_garbage_time`), which is what `{nba,wnba}_stats.possessions` serves once the producers' wiring (hoopR-nba-stats-data
  #54, wehoop-wnba-stats-data #28) is republished. `teams` is the stats schedule's home and away.
- **College** (`load_ncaa_wbb_possessions(2026)` filtered to `espn_game_id`, `load_wbb_schedule(2026)`): the release's
  rows as they are; bigballR's `is_garbage_time` is already in them. `teams` is the ESPN home and away ids.
- **`oracle`**: `situational_team`, `situational_player` and `situational_lineup` (`_common/situational_splits.py`) on
  `nba_situation_rows(...)` / `ncaa_situation_rows(...)` for the game, the `all` and `garbage` families only
  (`top_n=1` and empty ratings: the `opponent` family is not kept). The `team` rows carry the same values as the Data API's `situational_team_games` rows for 0022300718 and contest 6387150 (checked 2026-11-13), so the tests use them as the per-game splits the four factors read.
- **`names`**: for the 2023-24 game only (no BB-G1 capture covers it), `load_nba_stats_player_boxscores(2023)`'s
  `person_id, first_name, family_name, name_i`.

Games: TOR 100 at NOP 138, 2024-02-05 (`0022300718`, the game with the most garbage possessions, 53 of 193, in sdv-py's
committed BB-D7 corpus `tests/fixtures/bb_possession_flags/nba_possessions_2024.parquet`); GW 50 at Temple 86 (ESPN
401824983, 14 of 140, the `impact-box-wbb-2026` game); CON 75 at NY 106 (1022600001) and BOS 113 at DET 121
(0022600001), the BB-G1 pro games, neither with garbage time (bigballR's rule also needs three or fewer starters on).
The log's whole-game counts against stats.nba.com's team box (`load_*_stats_team_boxscores`): FGA, 3PA and FGM equal; FTA
within one (the log leaves the defense's technical free throws out); rebounds higher (the log counts team rebounds).

**Used by:** `test/garbageTime.test.ts`.

**To regenerate:** rerun those calls in an sdv-py checkout of `origin/main` (polars, no network beyond the GitHub
release assets), write `{...}` above with `json.dumps(..., default=str)` and gzip (`mtime=0`).

## `epv-box-{wnba,mbb,wbb}-2025.json.gz`
The rows behind BB-G46's EPV box (`resources/epvBox.ts` for the WNBA and college), one 2025 game a league. Built on
2026-11-10 with no Data API read (it was answering 429 that day): `players` and `teams` are the game's rows of sdv-db's
producer fixtures (`tests/fixtures/season_products/{wnba,mbb,wbb}_epv_{player,team}_games_2025.parquet` on sdv-db main
`6f125d3`, sdv-py's `{wnba,mbb}_epv_*` on the published releases), `season` and `game_id` dropped, no other edits; the
id and name rows are sportsdataverse-py `origin/main` loaders on the sportsdataverse-data releases, filtered to the game:

- **`epv-box-wnba-2025`**, LV at NY, 2025-05-17 (ESPN 401736116, stats 1022500005), as `{league, season, espnGameId,
  crosswalk, names, players, teams}`: `crosswalk` is `load_wnba_schedule_crosswalk(2025)`'s row (`wnba_game_id`,
  `wnba_home_team_id`, `wnba_away_team_id`), `names` the whole season's `load_wnba_player_crosswalk(2025)`
  (`wnba_player_id`, `wnba_player_name`), what `wnba.player_crosswalk?season=2025` serves. The stats box
  (`wnba_stats.player_box`) starts in 2026, so the season crosswalk names the WNBA rows.
- **`epv-box-{mbb,wbb}-2025`**, UNC Wilmington 67 at East Carolina 53, 2024-12-03 (ESPN 401722197, contest 5722015) and
  Winthrop 39 at Georgia Tech 85, 2024-11-04 (ESPN 401711537, contest 5722020), as `{league, season, espnGameId, home,
  away, box, players, teams, score}`: `box` is `load_ncaa_{mbb,wbb}_player_box(2025)`'s rows for the contest
  (`contest_id`, `player_id`, `clean_name`, `player`), what `ncaa_player_box?season=2025&espn_game_id=...` serves; `home`,
  `away` and `score` are `load_{mbb,wbb}_schedule(2025)`'s ESPN ids, names and scores.

Added 2026-11-13 for Q31's player links, captured live with exactly the Impact box's queries (the `data` arrays, no
edits), in all four `epv-box-*-2025` files: `pages` is `/v1/<nba_stats|wnba_stats|mbb|wbb>/shot_season_players?season=2025&select=person_id&limit=50000`
(566, 179, 4852 and 4516 rows), and college's `pairs` is `{<espn team id>: ncaa_player_crosswalk?season=2025&espn_team_id=…&select=ncaa_player_id,espn_athlete_id&limit=80}`
for each side (151 and 350; 59 and 2737). One player a college game has no crosswalk pair or page, so stays unlinked.

**Used by:** `test/epvBox.test.ts`.

**To regenerate:** rerun those calls in an sdv-py checkout (polars, no network beyond the GitHub release assets), filter to

## `wp-lenses-nba-{401704939,401704690}.json.gz`
Two 2025 NBA finals as the game page's Data API read sees them (`DataApiGameRows`: `schedule`, `pbp`, `team_box`,
`player_box`, `play_wp`, `game_team_rates`, `game_player_rates`), with BB-G45's two `play_wp` variant columns added.
CHA 98 at PHI 108, 2024-12-20 (401704939, closing line PHI -13, `game_lines.market_home_wp_close` 0.8424) and BKN 119 at
MEM 106, 2024-10-30 (401704690, no `game_lines` row): the BB-D33 games of sdv-db #217's own fixtures.

- **The seven tables**: read from the production Data API on 2026-11-10 (`GET /v1/nba/<table>?season=2025&game_id=<id>`,
  each with the `select` of `resources/nbaGames.ts`), as they are.
- **`home_win_prob_naive`, `home_win_prob_market`**: sdv-db #217 (merged 2026-11-10) adds them to `nba.play_wp`, but the
  Data API did not serve them yet when these were cut (`unknown select column`; the droplet backfill follows), so they
  were computed locally with sportsdataverse-py `nba_game_lines.wp_variants(pbp, market, league="nba",
  regulation_periods=4)` (4564898380) on sdv-db `tests/fixtures/nba_game_pages/nba_<id>_pbp.parquet` (the hoopR release's

  pbp reproduces the API's `home_win_prob` on every play exactly (max difference 0.0), so the variants are the build's.
